message.content:
The earliest non‑biblical references to Jesus Christ come from Roman and Jewish historians who lived within a few decades of his death.

| Author | Work | Date of Writing | Reference |
|--------|------|-----------------|-----------|
| **Flavius Josephus** | *Antiquities of the Jews* (Book 18, Chapter 3) | c. 93–94 CE | “...the wise man was called Jesus…he was crucified under Pontius Pilate during the reign of Tiberius.” |
| **Tacitus** | *Annals* (Book 15, Chapter 44) | c. 116 CE | “Christus, the founder of the name, was executed by Pontius Pilate.” |
| **Pliny the Younger** | Letter to Emperor Trajan (Letter 10.96) | c. 112 CE | Mentions early Christians worshipping “Christ” as a god. |

**Josephus’s passage** is considered the earliest because it was written only about 20–30 years after Jesus’s crucifixion. It appears in *Antiquities*, Book 18, Chapter 3, where Josephus briefly describes Jesus as a “wise man” and notes his execution by Pontius Pilate. This text has survived in Greek manuscripts and was later translated into Latin and other languages.

While some scholars debate whether the passage contains later Christian interpolation, most agree that the core reference to Jesus is authentic and provides the earliest independent historical attestation of his existence.
